newsitem.title: UK: Asian charterers take quality Mideast tankers.
newsitem.headline: Asian charterers take quality Mideast tankers.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering in the Middle East Gulf gathered steam on Thursday as a plethora of VLCCs found employment. Other chartering sectors took a back seat as the Middle East sector showed its dominance.

Shipping brokers said VLCCs to Japan were steady around W60 with South Korea discharges edging up a couple of points to W57.5. Asian charterers were noticeably active and the availability of good quality tonnage thinned.
"As expected both the Japanese and Koreans are taking the modern ships leaving the older tonnage," said one London broker.
In the Mediterranean 80,000 tonners began to weaken from a lack of interest.
"We have had a couple of suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) fixing, but only a few aframaxes (80,000 tonners)," said one Italian broker who said rates may ease to W90 from the current W97.5.
UK/continent fixing also showed steady rates around W100 on 80,000 toners going cross cont, but brokers said there was ample tonnage to meet anticipated demand.
The West African theatre saw 125,000 going to the U.S Gulf at W80 with 130,000 fixed to Spain at W80. "I don't expect any major changes," said one broker.
In the Caribbean up U.S. coast market rates were steady around W135-140.
Fuel oil tanker rates in the Baltic were seen to have eased.

"Shippers say there are less cargoes around and we are starting to approach the period when exports out of Russian close up," said a London-based broker. But he added that he expected fuel oil exports to continue throughout October.
Rates on 25,000 tonners were assessed around W225 from the W240 seem earlier in the week.
